content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Dayton

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and project-management experience before you apply. Review PMI's specific requirements for your background—whether you hold a bachelor's degree, associate degree, or high school diploma affects the hours of experience you'll need to demonstrate.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp, delivered by active certified practitioners. You'll attend instructor-led sessions online, covering the PMBOK® Guide framework, exam domains, and real-world application. This formal education satisfies PMI's mandatory contact-hour requirement.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing the bootcamp, create your PMI account and submit your PMP application with proof of your education and project experience. Pay the exam fee through PMI. You'll receive confirmation and eligibility to schedule your exam once PMI verifies your credentials.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Pass the PMP Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice tests, study guides, and instructor Q&A sessions—to reinforce your knowledge. Schedule your exam at a Pearson VUE testing center. You'll sit for the computer-based exam and receive your pass/fail result on the same day.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: Your PMP is valid for three years. During this cycle, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) by attending training, conferences, volunteer work, or publishing. Track your PDUs and renew your credential before expiration to keep your competitive edge in Dayton's aerospace, defense, healthcare, and manufacturing sectors.
